answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy makes membership expensive and trust gradual. Picture a vault that only opens for keys paid for in burned fees: every newcomer locks a deposit that vanishes if they cheat, so a thousand fake raven-winged identities cost a thousand real stakes. Then let reputation accrue slowly, like ivory growing in rings - each verified interaction adds a layer no shortcut can fake. Attacks stop being profitable when identity itself is collateral and history must be earned one honest season at a time.
